item.title: A Massachusetts farm stayed under one family's care for a century and was cultivated for 200 years
item.description: In a significant move towards sustainability, over 120 acres of Hoyt Farm in Essex have been shielded from commercial development, safeguarding its agricultural, forestry, and wildlife heritage. With cultivation practices dating back two centuries, this initiative, driven by local leaders and state agencies, secures essential natural resources and bolsters community food security, all while optimizing financial support to minimize town burden.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2019, a family moved a 255-year-old mansion 50 miles by barge to a new home
item.description: A 255-year-old mansion, Galloway House, was moved by a Maryland family to prevent it from being demolished. The structure traveled approximately 50 miles across the Chesapeake Bay after extensive planning and specialized equipment. Crews lifted the 400-ton house for a phased relocation that began in September 2019. After arriving at its new waterfront property in Queenstown, restoration efforts commenced to preserve its historic character.

item.title: Rob Scheer started Comfort Cases in 2013; it has given 300,000+ backpacks to foster kids
item.description: Comfort Cases, founded by Rob Scheer in 2013, helps provide essential items for children entering foster care. After experiencing the trauma of carrying trash bags, Scheer initiated a movement to change this narrative. The organization has distributed over 300,000 bags across multiple regions, including the US and the UK. It continually collaborates with community organizations to reach children in need effectively.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Utah crews remove 17 million tons of radioactive waste from Colorado River site
item.description: The Moab Uranium Mill Tailings Remedial Action Project has efficiently relocated 17 million tons of waste from the riverbank. Following rail transportation, teams are actively monitoring groundwater contamination levels. Upcoming efforts will also involve excavating contaminated soil near the original tailings site. The objective is to guarantee long-term safety and stability for local residents and the ecosystem. Ultimately, regrading and revegetating the area will be crucial in preventing future erosion.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Stephen King’s foundation helped heat Maine homes as radio fundraiser raised $241,820 for residents
item.description: In a generous act of support, Stephen King and Tabitha King donated $120,000 to a heating fundraiser aimed at aiding Maine families. This initiative, which garnered a total of $241,820, emerged in response to concerns regarding reduced federal assistance. Many households face the chilling threat of inadequate heating during the harsh winter months, highlighting the vital community spirit that seeks to protect those in financial hardship.

item.title: Effort to bring back the rapids of Grand Rapids that disappeared after industrial development
item.description: After nearly two decades of planning, construction is underway in downtown Grand Rapids to restore the historic rapids that gave the city its name. The first phase will remove four low-head dams and replace them with natural rock features designed to improve fish passage, habitat and river access. The project also includes measures to protect mussels and control invasive sea lampreys.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Iowa farmer says $25,000 wind lease is his farm's most profitable income source
item.description: In Iowa, a farmer discovered that collaborating with wind turbine projects resulted in a steadier income stream than conventional farming. This innovative approach combats the unpredictability of commodity prices and rising operational expenses. Numerous Midwestern farmers embrace this strategy, leading to sustainable financial growth. Wind energy initiatives also bolster local economies via enhanced tax revenues and infrastructure upgrades, demonstrating resilience despite some community pushback.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK-Iranian man arrested with link to security incident at US-run RAF Fairford base in England
item.description: A UK-Iranian dual national was arrested in London over a security incident linked to RAF Fairford. The incident followed the arrest of five British men suspected of preparing a terrorist act. Authorities are investigating potential foreign state involvement, particularly from Iran, which has denied any connection. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has indicated strong signs suggesting Iran's role in the incident.

item.title: American artist traded a painting and $10 for 153 acres in 1882; farm later became a landscape devoted to art
item.description: In 1882, Julian Alden Weir purchased a farm in Connecticut that transformed into his home and creative workspace. Initially focused on portraits and still life, he later immersed himself in the surrounding landscape. His shift towards Impressionism inspired numerous visiting artists. Today, the site is known as Weir Farm National Historical Park, preserving its artistic heritage with a collection of over 300 works reflecting American Impressionism.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Fatal point of no return’: Putin warns against use of nukes amid global tensions
item.description: Vladimir Putin expressed concerns about current global tensions and the potential for disastrous outcomes from escalating conflicts. He emphasized the importance of preventing the use of weapons of mass destruction in international disputes. Putin highlighted the role of Western technical support in Ukraine's military actions against Russia. He stated that Russia is not planning attacks on European countries but would respond to any aggression.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Linda Evangelista’s NYC penthouse sells for $6.75M after price cuts and Keanu Reeves rental
item.description: After a two-year sales journey, Linda Evangelista has sold her luxurious West Chelsea penthouse for $6.75 million. Originally priced at $9.45 million, the listing underwent several adjustments before finding a buyer. The penthouse is noted for its expansive layout and a sizable terrace, with celebrity appeal enhanced by Keanu Reeves' previous rental. Evangelista has since moved to a new apartment nearby, staying within New York's vibrant real estate scene.
